21. (Previously presented) A therapeutic training device comprising:a head mounted display comprising:
an outward facing video display comprising a transparency that is variable; and
a light having an adjustable brightness to illuminate eyes of a wearer,
wherein adjusting at least one of the transparency and the brightness allows an observer to see the eyes of the wearer through the outward facing video display.
22. (Previously presented) The therapeutic training device of claim 21, comprising a controller configured to inversely adjust the transparency of the outward facing video display and the brightness of the light.
23. (Previously presented) The therapeutic training device of claim 21, wherein the outward facing video display comprises a display selected from the group consisting of a video projector, a LCD display, a LED display, and a quantum dot display.
24. (Previously presented) The therapeutic training device of claim 21, wherein the outward facing video display comprises a plurality of outward facing video displays.
25. (Previously presented) The therapeutic training device of claim 21, further comprising eye tracking components and software.
26. (Previously presented) The therapeutic training device of claim 21, further comprising a controller configured to adjust the transparency of the outward facing video display, and to adjust the brightness of the light.
27. (Currently amended) A therapeutic training device, comprising:eyeglass frames;
an outward facing video display positioned within the eyeglass frames; and
a controller coupled to the outward facing video display to control a display of media content on the video display, wherein a level of the media content is selectively adjustable such that the display of media content and eyes of a user are each selectively viewable by a patient when the therapeutic training device is worn by the user,
wherein the outward facing video display is see-through from the side of the user.
28. (Previously presented) The device of claim 27, wherein the outward facing video display comprises a display selected from the group consisting of a video projector, a LCD display, a LED display, or a quantum dot display.
29. (Previously presented) The device of claim 27, wherein the outward facing video display comprises a plurality of outward facing video displays.
30. (Currently amended) The device of claim 27, wherein the level of the media content comprises a level of a characteristic selected from the group consisting of brightness, transparency, and opacity.
31. (Currently amended) The device of claim 27, wherein a visibility of the eyes of the user by the patient is variable based on the level of the media content displayed on the outward facing video display.
32. (Currently amended) The device of claim 31, wherein the level of the media content displayed on the outward facing video display is configured to be adjusted manually by the user.
33. (Currently amended) The device of claim 31, wherein the level of the media content displayed on the outward facing video display is configured to be adjusted by software.
34. (Currently amended) The device of claim 27, further comprising eye tracking components and software.
35. (Currently amended) The device of claim 31, wherein the device further comprises a light having an adjustable brightness and configured to illuminate eyes of the user to increase the visibility of the eyes of the user by the patient.
36. (Currently amended) The device of claim 35, further comprising a controller configured to inversely adjust the level of the media content displayed on the outward facing video display and the brightness of the light.
